column1: # ci/red-arms/batch15-spotcheck.tsv -- TEXTUAL spot-checks for #289 batch 15.
# Feed to:  bash ci/pump-red-arm.sh linux-clang-debug ci/red-arms/batch15-spotcheck.tsv
# ⚠️ THESE ARMS PARTITION ON THE MISS BRANCH'S RETURN DISPOSITION, which is the axis
# this batch actually varies. Batches 13/14 migrated sites in void test bodies, where
# every miss branch does the same three things and one arm per enclosing CONTEXT was
# the informative split. Every site here is inside a helper that RETURNS A VALUE, so
# the question each site had to answer is "what does the miss branch return, and does
# the caller notice?" -- and a wrong answer there is SILENT at the call site rather
# than at the site itself. One arm per distinct answer:
#   run_sync                        free helper, explicit trailing return type; the
#                                   sentinel converts implicitly
#   MinimalSession::run_coro        member helper, `auto` return; needs `using R =
#                                   decltype(fut.get())` because two returns of
#                                   DIFFERENT types do not deduce
#   drive_to_active/open            a bool channel that already existed
#   ReconcileFixture::drive/send    a struct FIELD poisoned -- a default-constructed
#                                   `expected_t<void>` HAS a value, so the arm proves
#                                   the poison, not just the early return
#   make_reconnect_initiator/open   returns the fixture VALID; callers deref it
#                                   unconditionally, so null would be a crash
#   open_to_active/open             the settled void recipe, unchanged; the control
#                                   that this batch did not break the ordinary case
# ⚠️ COLUMN 6 (exec stem) IS LOAD-BEARING FOR NEARLY EVERY ROW HERE, and its absence
# would have read as a defect. The driver asserts the arm's own test RAN by matching
# the label's stem against `[ RUN ]` lines, which works only while a label names a
# test. These labels name HELPERS with no single test to be named after, so without
# column 6 every row would report INCONCLUSIVE for a reason about naming rather than
# about the site. The column, and this consequence,
# were added in this same change; see ci/pump-red-arm.sh's arms-file docs.
# ⚠️ NO `fuzz_admin_parse/*` ARM. Those three sites report NOTHING by design (see
# ci/red-arms/batch15-labels.txt), so a textual arm on them would assert the absence
# of a report and pass whether or not the site was mutated -- an arm that cannot go
# RED. They are covered by the seam arm, where SILENT is the DOCUMENTED expectation.
# ⚠️ AN ANCHOR ON AN ENCLOSING FUNCTION FORCES THAT FUNCTION'S *FIRST* SITE, NOT THE
# ONE YOU NAMED. Measured here, not hypothesised: the `ReconcileFixture::drive/send`
# row first anchored on `Driven drive(...)`, the function signature. `drive()` holds
# THREE migrated sites, so the driver forced the first (`/open`), whose miss branch
# returned early and masked the other two -- and the run reported "NO REPORT ... This IS
# a finding about the site" for `/send`, which is a WRONG VERDICT AGAINST CORRECT CODE
# (the seam arm had already proven `/send` RED independently). The driver's own arms-file
# contract says the anchor must be "on or just above the `run_window_then_ready(` call to
# force"; a signature line satisfies "unique" and violates "just above". Anchor on the
# `co_spawn` immediately above the call instead.
# [[feedback_force_each_red_arm_individually_an_early_return_masks_later_sites]]
# Rows here still anchored on a signature are valid ONLY while the label names that
# function's FIRST site. That is a condition, not a fact, so re-derive it rather than
# trusting this sentence -- for each row, the first label after the anchor must equal
# the row's own label:
#   python3 - <<'EOF'
#   import re
#   for f,a,l in [...]:   # (file, anchor, label) from the rows below
#       s=open(f).read(); i=s.index(a)
#       print(l, re.search(r'run_window_then_ready\s*\([^;]*?"([^"]+)"', s[i:], re.S).group(1))
#   EOF
